source: EPRA Approved Retail Electricity Tariff (2023/24 – 2025/26) — Domestic Consumer (DC1 / DC2 / DC3)
fixedChargeNote: EPRA abolished the monthly KES 150 fixed standing charge for domestic prepaid consumers

levies.repLevyLabel: Rural Electrification Programme (REP) Levy (5% of base energy)

fuelCostCharge.label: Fuel Energy Cost Charge (FCC) per kWh — gazetted monthly by EPRA
fuelCostCharge.note: Varies monthly based on thermal generation mix and global fuel prices

forexAdjustment.label: Foreign Exchange Rate Fluctuation Adjustment (FERFA) per kWh — gazetted monthly

notes: Under the EPRA 2023–2026 Retail Tariff Review, there is no monthly fixed standing charge (KES 0) for domestic consumers
Domestic Lifeline (DC1) covers the first 30 kWh/month at KES 12.14/kWh base energy rate
Domestic Ordinary (DC2) covers 31–100 kWh/month at KES 16.50/kWh base energy rate
Consumption above 100 kWh/month (DC3) is billed at KES 19.07/kWh base energy rate
Each kWh also attracts Fuel Energy Cost (FCC), Forex Adjustment (FERFA), Inflation Adjustment (IA), EPRA Levy (KES 0.18), WRA Levy (KES 0.05), 5% REP Levy, and 16% VAT
